summary: Relaying reference notes the user pasted (summary of an Uber Maps talk by Karan Parikh on HMM map matching). Forwarded as background for your HMM design; your call how/if to use it. Cite it in docs/repository-references-ml.md only if you actually use it.

details.source: User-pasted summary of a talk video (no URL given). Treat as secondary material, not a citation-ready source.
points: Road network as directed graph: intersections = vertices, street segments = edges.
Distances: great-circle/haversine between points vs shortest-path (Dijkstra) distance along the road network respecting direction/rules.
Problem: noisy, sparse GPS (lat, lon, speed, course) -> positions on physical road segments; online (dispatch) vs offline (post-trip, fare) use cases. Ours is offline.
Candidates: K nearest road segments per GPS point via a geospatial index (e.g. R-tree).
Emission: likelihood from great-circle distance between GPS point and its projection on the candidate road (Gaussian-style).
Transition: exponential distribution favouring feasible routes (classic formulation: on |great-circle distance between consecutive points - route distance between their projections|).
Viterbi: dynamic programming for the most probable hidden road sequence.
details.relevance_note: This matches the standard Newson & Krumm (2009) formulation. Our contract already expects emissions from the selected classifier's outputs (not distance alone) plus graph transitions; a distance-only geometric HMM could serve as your non-ML decoder baseline/M1 diagnostic and as a comparison for classifier-emission HMM.
